root_motivation: WHO: Joe as operator of mcphost-1 when he is not at a shell, and synthorg's mtproof probe, which only reaches the host over MCP. WHAT: the signup kill switch is a file the host already reads, but nothing over MCP can create or remove it, so the mtproof kill_switch link refuses on every chain run. WHY: PRD-mcphost-signup-kill-switch-and-source requirement 8 named the tool and never had an AC, so it was never built.
user_persona: An operator (or the probe acting for them) holding the admin key who must pause and resume signups with one MCP call each, audited, and restore the host with one call if a sequence dies halfway.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a test server with the admin key, When the admin lists tools, Then `admin.signup_pause` is listed with `message` (string), `resume` (boolean), `until` (integer), its description says exactly one of `message` or `resume: true` is required, the arms-equal-descriptors drift test passes, and README.md § signup names the tool.

Given no pause file, When the admin calls `admin.signup_pause` with a message, Then the pause file holds it as line 1, the result is `{paused: true, changed: true, message, retry_after_secs: 3600}`, healthz reports `signups_enabled: false` plus the message, and `signup` returns `signup_paused` with it; a hand-written file is replaced the same way.

Given a pause file written by the tool or by hand, When the admin calls `admin.signup_pause` with `resume: true`, Then the file is gone, the result is `{paused: false, changed: true}`, healthz reports `signups_enabled: true` with no `signup_pause_message`, and a `signup` succeeds.

Given calls with no arguments, both `message` and `resume: true`, `resume: false` alone, an empty message, a newline in the message, a message over 512 bytes, and `until` not in the future, When the admin makes each, Then each returns `invalid_params` naming the field and the pause file is unchanged.

Given a tenant key and an anonymous client, When each calls `admin.signup_pause`, Then each is refused with the same error code every other `admin.*` tool returns to that caller (`forbidden` for a tenant key), no pause file is created, and healthz still reports `signups_enabled: true`.

Given no pause file, When the admin calls `resume: true` twice, Then both return `{paused: false, changed: false}`; and Given `MCPHOST_SIGNUP_PAUSE_FILE` points into a missing directory, When the admin pauses, Then the error code is `storage`, nothing panics, and healthz answers `signups_enabled: true`.

Given 20 concurrent admin calls (10 distinct messages, 10 resumes), When all complete, Then every call succeeded, no `status()` read saw a truncated file, the final state agrees with healthz, and `admin.audit_log` holds 10 `signup_pause` and 10 `signup_resume` rows with `actor_key_id`.

Given `message: "window"` and `until` 600 s ahead, When paused, Then the file's line 2 is `until=<ts>`, the result and `signup`'s error carry `retry_after_secs` within 2 s of 600, and alerts `signup.paused` and `signup.resumed` are raised within `PAUSE_POLL_INTERVAL_SECS` + 2 s.

scope: src/handler.rs: the `admin.signup_pause` descriptor in `admin_tools_raw` and its `dispatch_admin_tool` arm; src/admin.rs: `signup_pause`, argument validation and the `admin_audit_entry` arm; src/state.rs: `SignupPause::pause` (atomic temp-file rename) and `resume` writers; README.md § signup via docs/agent-quickstart.md and the regenerated www/llms.txt.
non_goals: Any change to how `signup` decides it is paused, to healthz fields, to alert keys or to the `signup_paused` error code; a default expiry on a tool-set pause; scheduled or per-source pauses; any synthorg change; hand-editing www/llms.txt.

additional.no_schema_change: No migration, schema change or new env var: the tool only writes the file `SignupPause::status` already reads.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the mtproof kill_switch link refuse on every chain run?
five_whys_trace.a: Its preflight requires admin.signup_pause in the admin tools/list, and the tool does not exist.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does the tool not exist?
five_whys_trace.a: PRD-mcphost-signup-kill-switch-and-source listed it as requirement 8 (P2) with no acceptance criterion.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did a missing AC let the requirement go unbuilt?
five_whys_trace.a: The builder derives its tests from ACs, so a requirement without one is never proven nor demanded.

five_whys_trace.q: Why can an operator not just touch the file?
five_whys_trace.a: The probe cannot ssh and Joe off a shell has no path to the data dir; SignupPause had no writer.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Which error code do argument-validation failures carry?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: `invalid_params` via AppError::InvalidParams, not the descriptor precheck's `args_invalid`, so the descriptor declares types only and the handler enforces the 1..=512 byte, one-line and future-`until` rules.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Is a resume that removed no file still audited?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Yes: AC7 counts one `signup_resume` row per resume call, so the audit arm is unconditional on `changed`.
